questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The table shows the total utility that an individual derives from consuming different quantities of a good. quantity of total utility good (units) (units)
62 The individual’s marginal utility of money is $1 = 2 units of utility. What is the maximum quantity of the good that the individual will buy when its price is $6?

options.A: 2 units B 3 units C 4 units D 5 units

questions.questionText: In the diagram, XY is a firm’s total cost curve. Y total costs X O output What happens to the firm’s costs as output is increased? average average fixed costs variable costs
What is most likely to pose a threat to the survival of small local bakeries?

options.A: an increase in the cost per minute of television advertising
options.B: a switch in consumer preferences to cheaper mass-produced bread
options.C: diseconomies of scale in the process of bread production

questions.questionText: The demand for a firm’s product is perfectly elastic. What will be the effect on the firm’s revenue if it increases its price by 5%?

options.C: Its revenue will fall to zero.

questions.questionText: A perfectly competitive industry becomes a profit-maximising monopoly. The marginal cost curve of the monopolist is identical to the supply curve of the perfectly competitive industry. How will output and price be affected? output price
A firm earns supernormal profit when its profit is

options.A: above that earned by competing firms.
options.B: above that needed to cover its fixed costs.
options.C: above that needed to keep the firm in production in the short run.
options.D: above that required to keep its resources in their present use in the long run.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an industry’s supply and demand curves. S u v price w x D O Q quantity The government initially restricts the quantity to OQ. The restriction on the quantity is then removed. In the absence of externalities, which area in the diagram measures the net gain in economic welfare?

options.A: u B v C v + w D v + w + x

What adjustments to real GNP per head might make it a more reliable indicator when comparing standards of living in different countries?

options.A: adjustments to allow for differences in population size in different countries
options.B: adjustments to allow for differences in rates of inflation in different countries
options.C: adjustments to allow for differences in the relative size of the hidden economy in different countries
options.D: the use of market exchange rates rather than purchasing power parity exchange rates

questions.questionText: Which combination of circumstances is most likely to lead to an increase in a country’s budget deficit? discretionary total GDP unemployment government spending
Which correctly identifies injections into a country’s circular flow of income? private sector public sector trade sector (S > I) (T > G) (X > M)

A closed economy with no government has a marginal propensity to consume of 0.9. Its full employment national income is $60000m. Its current national income is $40000m. To achieve full employment, by how much must investment be increased?

What will result from a rise in interest rates?

options.A: a depreciation in the exchange rate
options.B: a fall in the price of bonds
options.D: an increase in the demand for money

questions.questionText: In which circumstance will an increase in the public sector deficit not lead to an increase in the money supply, other things being equal?

options.A: Commercial bank lending to the private sector is held constant.
options.B: The deficit is financed by an increase in government borrowing from private individuals.
options.C: The rate of interest is held constant.

questions.questionText: What is meant by liquidity preference?

options.A: a desire to be paid in cash rather than by cheque
options.B: a desire to be paid monthly rather than weekly
options.C: a desire to hold assets that are convertible into cash
options.D: a desire to hold money rather than other assets

questions.questionText: Which combination is usually found in developing countries?

options.A: a low birth rate and a dominant primary sector
options.B: capital intensive production and a rapidly growing population
options.C: external debt and a low death rate
options.D: labour intensive production and a low rate of saving

questions.questionText: Which pattern of labour market data is likely to indicate an increase in cyclical unemployment? changes in compulsory voluntary redundancies resignations
What would an economist include when using social cost-benefit analysis to assess policies to reduce the level of unemployment? changes in changes in changes in crime rates mental health work skills
The diagram shows the short-run trade-off between a country’s inflation rate and its national output level. + rate of inflation O national output – What could cause the curve to shift to the left?

options.A: an increase in the money supply
options.C: an increase in the expected future rate of inflation
options.D: an increase in the budget deficit
